title: dedicated autoscaler: add backpressure controls and enhance utilization reporting
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring tail latency spikes on Dedicated fleets when transient load bursts exhausted token-bucket credits and caused aggressive scale-up followed by noisy neighbor effects. This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) a backpressure controller that applies short-lived soft-shed and request-prioritization during token-bucket exhaustion to stabilize latency and reduce unnecessary scale churn, and 2) improved utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets so SRE/Platform teams can better correlate burst events with autoscaler decisions.

What this PR does: - Adds a BackpressureController in the dedicated autoscaler that: - monitors token-bucket state, queue depth, and recent per-fleet P50/P95 latency trends - applies configurable soft-shed (percent of low-priority requests) and an adaptive priority multiplier to high-priority routes - exposes metrics for backpressure_active, shed_rate, and applied_priority_multiplier - Adds quota and smoothing knobs to the token-bucket allocator (smoother refill and burst window limits) to reduce sudden credit depletion - Enhances the utilization reporting pipeline: - new metrics: fleet_effective_utilization, burst_recharge_time_seconds, queued_request_count_by_priority - emits per-fleet daily summaries and per-burst window samples to observability (prometheus + tracing tags) - Updates the autoscaler policy config schema to include backpressure thresholds and rollout flags - Adds integration tests + a small simulation harness to verify behavior under synthetic burst patterns

Rollout plan: Feature guarded behind runtime flag dedicated.autoscaler.backpressure.enabled (default off). Initial rollout will target Canary fleets in us-west-2 for 48h, followed by staged enabling on small Dedicated customers. Observability dashboards and on-call runbook updated.

Performance: Local simulation and canary runs on 3 fleets showed: - 35% reduction in p95 tail latency during sustained burst windows - 22% fewer scale-up events attributed to token-bucket exhaustion - marginal CPU increase on autoscaler process (~4%) which is acceptable given the reduction in downstream GPU churn

Related: ENG-4982 (backpressure design), ENG-4991 (utilization reporting), SUP-3421 (customer incident that motivated smoothing).

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e simulation harness - [x] updated runbooks and dashboards - [x] rollout plan

Notes: This change is conservative and opt-in. We purposely keep backpressure as a soft mitigation to avoid dropping critical traffic. Future follow-ups will add automated canary promotion and finer-grained per-tenant policies.

review_comments: Mateo Rivera: Strong design. Can we add a safety cap so shed_rate never exceeds 40% by default?
Ava Chen: Added a safety cap config and documented default in schema_v2.yaml; updated tests to assert cap.
Priya Nair: Please add an e2e that demonstrates priority multiplier effect on low-priority routes.
Ava Chen: Added simulation test and CI integration that exercises priority routing under burst load.
Lucas Ford: Observability looks good. Can you tag the new metrics with fleet_id and customer_tier?

release_notes: Add optional backpressure controls to Dedicated autoscaler; smoothing for token-bucket refill; enhanced per-fleet utilization metrics and dashboards.
notes_for_oncall: If backpressure_active spikes > 15% of requests for > 10m, consider disabling dedicated.autoscaler.backpressure.enabled and investigate token-bucket refill anomalies. Dashboards: Dedicated Autoscaler Overview -> Backpressure tab.
changelog_summary: Opt-in backpressure and utilization reporting improvements to reduce autoscaler churn and tail latency during bursts.
